### msleep questions

```{r, message=FALSE}

### Q1: Use filter() to subset msleep to only animals who are awake for at least 12 hours of the day.

library(dbplyr)

filter(msleep, sleep_total > 12)

### Q2: Use mutate() to create a new column called percent_day_awake that gives the percentage of the day that each species spends awake. Use select() with everything() at the end to verify your calculation.

percent_day_awake <- msleep |> 
  mutate(percent_day_awake = awake / 24 * 100) |> 
  select(name, sleep_total, awake, percent_day_awake)

percent_day_awake

# Removed some columns so it's easier to read when I knit.

```
### Storm Tracking Questions

```{r, warning=FALSE}

### Q4: Use filter() to subset storms to only storms with wind speeds greater than 50 knots, then use arrange() to sort by wind descending.

filter(storms, wind > 50) |> 
  arrange(desc(wind)) |> 
  select(year, wind)


# I'm selecting these columns because it knits weird if I use all of them. 

```

### Site preference questions

```{r, message=FALSE}

#Setup
library(dplyr)
lizards
# View(lizards)

# Q5: Determine which Site and Diameter combination has the highest total grahami.

# group Site and Diameter, then I'll create a new lizard variable. Getting error because of missing values...
# na.rm for when missing values is true

library(dplyr)

lizards |> 
  group_by(Site, Diameter) |> 
  summarise(total_grahami = sum(grahami, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  arrange(desc(total_grahami))

# Shade and D <=2 has the largest concentration of grahami lizards.


# Q6: Create a boxplot showing the distribution of opalinus counts under different light conditions (Sun vs. Shade) using ggplot2.

ggplot(lizards, aes(x = Site, y = opalinus, fill = Site)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of opalinus counts by varying light condition",
       x = "Light condition", y = "Opalinus count") +
  theme_minimal()

# This is absolutely horrid but it its what it is.


```
